main_body: A 4x3-tile farm ground patch: a wheat band on top, a green crop-row band, then tilled soil furrows with sprouts. It is a flat ground surface seen from above.
top_band: none. This is a flat terrain patch, not a standing object. The column runs through wheat (rows 0-14), crop greens (16-22) and soil furrows (24+).
evidence: The kind is terrain, so the standing-object top-plus-front contract does not apply. The drawing reads as a ground surface made of horizontal bands (wheat, crops, tilled soil) with no standing volume and no receding side faces. It is not a front-elevation object, so I treat it as acceptable terrain.

style.evidence: Each material has about 4-5 lightness steps. Wheat runs gold, bright yellow, cream, ochre and brown, and a checker dither gives it grain. The crop greens use 4 tones in clumps. The soil uses 4-5 browns with lighter clods and green sprouts. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines are tinted dark brown or green (dark_material_tone). Flat-fill coverage is 0%. At 13 colours per tile it is below the grass reference (26) but well above the paving reference (7). Its 24 distinct colours are fewer than the grass reference's 80 but more than the paving's 7. That makes it somewhat lower than the grass, but the tiles are textured rather than flat or sticker-like, so it sits acceptably next to the references.
